graders.name: reproduce-first
graders.evidence:
`getUser` returns `session.user`, and `login` immediately does `user.id` — if a session has no `user` (expired/invalid/anonymous session), `getUser` returns `undefined` and `login` crashes with exactly the reported `TypeError: cannot read properties of undefined (reading 'id')`.

graders.name: reproduce-first
graders.evidence:
Found and fixed it. Two things worth flagging:

1. **No git history is available here** — there's no `.git` directory and `git` itself is blocked in this sandbox, so I couldn't confirm which Tuesday commit actually introduced the regression. The subagent verified this independently too.
2. **The whole app is just `src/auth.js`** (8 lines) — `getUser(session)` returned `session.user` unconditionally, and `login()` immediately did `user.id`. Whenever `session.user` is missing (unauthenticated/expired session, or the session shape changed upstream), that throws exactly the `TypeError: cannot read properties of undefined (reading 'id')` you're seeing.

Fix applied in `src/auth.js:1-11`: `getUser` now guards against a missing `session`, and `login` throws a clear `"No authenticated user in session"` error instead of crashing on the raw property access. This stops the page-crashing TypeError, but whatever renders the login page still needs to catch that error and show a proper "please sign in again" state rather than letting it bubble up — that caller isn't part of this repo, so you'll want to point me at it (or the actual production repo) if you want that wired up too.

graders.name: reproduce-first
reproduce-first
graders.evidence:
I patched `src/auth.js:5-10` so `login` no longer crashes with a raw `TypeError` — it now throws a clear `login failed: no authenticated user in session` error instead.

That said, this repo only contains `src/auth.js` and `package.json` — there's no session-creation/middleware code here, and `git log` isn't runnable in this sandbox (git binary is permission-denied), so I can't see what changed in Tuesday's deploy. The real root cause is upstream: something is now calling `login(session)` with a session that has no `.user` set (expired session, auth middleware ordering change, cookie/token parsing failure, etc.). My fix stops the crash and gives you a diagnosable error message, but you'll want to find why `session.user` is missing — check whatever sets `session.user` before `login` is called, and see what changed there Tuesday.
